what: q3h central-SU reference latency (HANDOFF item 6) vs the Q-DV slice root, per RMSNorm and per layer

run.dut: ot_hdc_vstream_static_entries SW64 LV7 ML15 LT1 LOFF1 RD2 RED_ENTRIES1 (the TP8 compute die SU64 core)

dv_edges.note_psum: bench (g): issue->last PSUM 163 for 96 beats and 83 for 16 beats (cmd->first issue included, so an upper bound)

notes: the ledger (cycles_dv.py) counts the DV scalar-tree wire hops N and treats in-unit root compute as cancelling; this adds the measured compute difference
the earlier ~24-cycle q3h estimate counted only the in-unit tree; the q3h path also pays a full separate rsqrt SU op (117 edges at ML 15)

q3h op 2 is issued on the first ready edge after SSX is written; a static schedule could issue it up to the go->read offset earlier (a few edges), so the per-norm gain is a few edges optimistic at most
rough rate: -66 cyc/layer priced +0.96 % tok/s, so -336 is about +5 % tok/s by the same scaling (to be re-priced in the model)
